newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Bamerindus to get special aid - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Bamerindus to get special aid - paper.

text.p: A resolution approved by Brazil's National Monetary Council (CMN) last Thursday will help out private bank Bamerindus to overcome its liquidity troubles, newspapers said on Tuesday.

The CMN approved a special credit line, which does not require transfer of a controlling interest, earmarked for banks with liquidity problems but without showing a negative net worth, said columnist Celso Pinto at Folha de Sao Paulo daily.
So far the federal government has granted credits to banks needing restructuring which were conditioned on a complete change of ownership.
The credit line would satisfy Bamerindus majority shareholder Senator Jose Eduardo Andrade Vieira.
Vieira, a powerful ally of President Fernando Henrique Cardoso, has thus far refused to consider giving up control of Bamerindus, despite the bank's recognized liquidity troubles.
According to Celso Pinto, the resolution says there is no limit for the special credit line which "will depend on the real needs of the financial institution and the guarantees offered."
In the case of Bamerindus, the bank's balance sheet shows it needs some 1.9 billion reais to return to December 1994's liquidity levels.
Celso Pinto also said the credit line would be valid for 90 days but renewable at the request of the bank and following Central Bank criteria.
Bamerindus, Brazil's fourth-largest private bank, has been struggling to recover liquidity, restore public confidence and fight speculation that the bank would be sold.
